key_insight: The paper combines a lower-cost quantum ansatz with a generative ML subspace model to make selected configuration interaction more efficient for molecular simulation in the NISQ-to-fault-tolerant transition.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical hybrid workflow for reducing classical preprocessing and improving scalability in quantum chemistry pipelines relevant to drug-discovery workloads.
method: LCNot-UCCSD replaces the higher-order LUCJ initialization with MP2-based parameter setup, reducing scaling from O(N^6) to O(N^4).
QSCI-RBM swaps SQD configuration recovery for a Restricted Boltzmann Machine to generate a compact candidate subspace.
The workflow is tested in QARP on a state-vector simulator and embedded in DMET for larger molecular systems.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate eight molecules over 14 artificial error levels with 100 independent runs each, and further validate on N2 PES scans plus DMET applications to Amantadine and the SARS-CoV-2 main protease complex with Carmofur.
watch_item: Results are simulator-based, so real hardware noise, error mitigation overheads, and RBM generalization quality may change performance in practice.
paper_title: Bridging the NISQ and Fault-Tolerant Regimes: Generative-ML-Assisted Quantum Selected CI for Molecular Simulations
